newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 12.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The airplane style "black box" recovered from the Watford rail crash was not working at the time of impact "due to lack of maintenance". Crash investigators hoped that the device would uncover the events which led up to the crash which left one woman dead and 68 commuters injured.
TUNNEL DEBT TALKS HIT CONVERSION SNAG
Negotiations between Eurotunnel and bankers aimed at restructuring the company' nine billion stg debt have hit a snag over the conversion price of securities which would be part of the deal.

Eurotunnel bosses are holding out for a conversion rate of around 265p, the price of its last rights issue in 1994, however, Eurotunnel units currently trade at 101.5p. The proposed deal involves an equity swap which would give the banks 49 per cent of Eurotunnel equity.
AUSSIE MINERS TAKE A COPPER BEATING
Continuing poor metal prices have led to a sharp fall in the share prices of mining concerns RTZ-CTA and BHP on the Australian stock exchange.
ALL EYES ON U.S. INTEREST RATE POINTERS

Speculation from dealers about the possibility an early rise in U.S. interest rates now centre on the size of the hike rather than its probability. A survey from the Federal Reserve Board, indicated that the rise could be low, as regional inflationary pressures were kept in check.
